editorial:
Imagine jumping back in time to the very start of cinema. You get to see a young peasant girl who hears voices from God and decides she is the only one who can save France from its enemies. It feels more like a stage play than a modern movie, but that is part of the charm. The vibe is very dreamy and old-school, with bright costumes and bold acting that makes the whole story feel like a legendary fairy tale coming to life right in front of you.

What really stands out is how the director uses simple tricks to make magic happen on screen. Since it is from 1900, the acting is very over-the-top, but it keeps things moving quickly. You might find the lack of sound a bit weird at first, but you can easily follow the plot.
endingExplained: The story reaches a sad peak when Joan is captured by her enemies. After a long trial where she is treated unfairly, the movie shows her being sentenced to death. The final scenes show her being burned at the stake. It is a heartbreaking end, but it wraps up by showing her as a martyr who died for her faith and her country, leaving a legacy that people still talk about today.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves the history of film and old stories.
